sections.text: [serious] Breast biopsies are read in the order they arrive. [dramatic] So an invasive cancer can sit in line... behind a stack of benign cases.

[confident] Sepia reorders the queue. Uni two H, a pathology foundation model, reads every image through a calibrated probe. Frozen sections go first. Then anything where invasive can't be ruled out. Then the low-confidence reads.
[lively] Open a case. The read is linear, so the invasive score is the exact sum of each region's contribution. The heatmap shows precisely what the model used.

This one reads seventy-three percent invasive. [dramatic] ...It's actually in situ. [confident] But in situ never left the ninety-percent confidence set. So Sepia flagged it, and drafted P sixty-three and calponin: the stains that separate the two.
Every feature it cites passed an AI spot check. Mitotic figures failed, zero of twenty, so they're never given as a reason.

Nothing is ordered until the pathologist approves. [serious] For frozen sections, the surgeon sees a timer, never the model's read, until the pathologist calls the margin. And unfamiliar inputs raise a reliability flag that says: defer.

[confident] On a hundred thirty-two held-out images, all thirty-one invasive cases were caught, at ninety-seven percent specificity. On external TCGA slides: ninety-six percent of FFPE tumors... and eighty-four percent of frozen sections.
[warm] Sepia orders the queue and shows its work. The pathologist makes every call.
